items.stem: AB is a tangent to a circle with centre O at A, and AC is a chord with ∠BAC = 64°. Find ∠OAC.
A tangent PQ at a point P of a circle of radius 9 cm meets a line through the centre O at Q. If ∠PQO = 25°, find ∠POQ.
Prove that the tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact.
items.answer: Let XY be the tangent at P. Take any point Q ≠ P on XY; Q lies outside the circle, so OQ > OP. Thus OP is the shortest distance from O to XY, hence OP ⟂ XY.
items.markingKey: Figure (1), any other point outside (1), OQ > OP (1), shortest distance is perpendicular (1), conclusion (1).

items.stem: Prove that the tangents drawn at the ends of a diameter of a circle are parallel.
items.answer: Tangents at A and B are perpendicular to diameter AB; two lines perpendicular to the same line are parallel (alternate/co-interior angles 90°).
items.markingKey: Key points: Tangents at A and B are perpendicular to diameter AB; two lines perpendicular to the same line are parallel (alternate/co-interior angles 90°). Award 5 marks for a complete, correctly reasoned answer.

items.stem: A circular fountain in a park has radius 80 m. A straight footpath touches the fountain's boundary at point P. A lamp post L stands on the path 60 m from P. (i) What is the angle between the radius OP and the path? Why? (ii) Find the distance OL. (iii) Is the lamp post inside or outside the fountain? (iv) How many such straight paths through L can touch the fountain?
items.answer: (i) 90°, the tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact (ii) 100 m (iii) outside, since 100 > 80 (iv) 2

items.stem: Prove that the perpendicular at the point of contact to the tangent to a circle passes through the centre.
items.answer: The radius at the point of contact is perpendicular to the tangent; there is only one perpendicular at that point, so it contains the radius and hence the centre.
items.markingKey: Key points: The radius at the point of contact is perpendicular to the tangent; there is only one perpendicular at that point, so it contains the radius and hence the centre. Award 5 marks for a complete, correctly reasoned answer.

items.stem: Explain why no tangent can be drawn to a circle from a point inside it.
items.answer: Any line through an interior point cuts the circle at two points (it is a secant).
